experiments.command: ./bench --method slope --unroll 800 --unroll2 1600 --iters 40 --warmup 10 --reps 5 --init 'addi.d $r20, $sp, -1024; li.d $r22, -64; and $r20, $r20, $r22; li.d $r4, 8; st.b $r4, $r20, 0; li.d $r4, 0; st.b $r4, $r20, 8; li.d $r5, 0; addi.d $r4, $r20, 0' --asm 'ldgt.b $r4, $r4, $r0; add.d $r4, $r4, $r20'
experiments.name: base operand path

latencies.notes: 4 cycles from the base operand rj to the destination, the same latency as a plain load of the same width. The chain has to turn the loaded value back into an address with an add.d, and it also carries one further cycle that the address generator charges for an ALU-produced address, so 2 cycles are subtracted. That extra cycle belongs to the chain, not to the load.

experiments.command: ./bench --method slope --unroll 800 --unroll2 1600 --iters 40 --warmup 10 --reps 5 --init 'addi.d $r20, $sp, -1024; li.d $r22, -64; and $r20, $r20, $r22; li.d $r4, 8; st.b $r4, $r20, 0; li.d $r4, 0; st.b $r4, $r20, 8; li.d $r5, 0; li.d $r4, 0' --asm 'ldgt.b $r4, $r20, $r4'
experiments.name: index/bound operand path

latencies.notes: 4 cycles from the index or bound operand rk to the destination. When the loaded value can feed the address or the range check directly the chain is just the load; when an andi or xori is in the path it reads one cycle more than the helper itself, which is the address-generator premium rather than load latency.

throughput.name: 8 independent addresses
throughput.command: ./bench --unroll 1000 --iters 1000 --warmup 10 --reps 5 --core 0 --init 'addi.d $r20, $sp, -1024; addi.d $r21, $r20, 0; addi.d $r23, $r20, 8; addi.d $r24, $r20, 16; addi.d $r25, $r20, 24; addi.d $r26, $r20, 32; addi.d $r27, $r20, 40; addi.d $r28, $r20, 48; addi.d $r29, $r20, 56; addi.d $r30, $r20, -8; addi.d $r4, $r0, 1; addi.d $r5, $r0, 2; addi.d $r6, $r0, 3; addi.d $r7, $r0, 4; addi.d $r8, $r0, 5; addi.d $r9, $r0, 6; addi.d $r10, $r0, 7; addi.d $r11, $r0, 8' --asm 'ldgt.b $r12, $r21, $r30; ldgt.b $r13, $r23, $r30; ldgt.b $r14, $r24, $r30; ldgt.b $r15, $r25, $r30; ldgt.b $r16, $r26, $r30; ldgt.b $r17, $r27, $r30; ldgt.b $r18, $r28, $r30; ldgt.b $r19, $r29, $r30'
throughput.notes: 8 independent lanes: 7.98 core cycles per 8 instructions, CPI 1. Slope method (--unroll 1000, --unroll2 2000).

notes: 4 cycles, the same for every width and for both the base and the index or bound operand. The load result is available four cycles after the address, and a chain that passes it through an ALU operation before using it as the next address reads one cycle more than that operation, which is what the address generator charges for an ALU-produced address rather than load latency.
